subject: Commit-linked support ladder & incident credit negotiation
messages:
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@skywardanalytics.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: SLA packaging options for enterprise commit

Hi Irene / Ben,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look promising for our forecasted load. Procurement asked me to get a concise summary of support options tied to annual commit levels. Specifically: 
- We need 99.95%+ availability guarantees for inference in us-west (our prod region).
- Faster response times (P1: 1 hour acknowledgment, 4-hr target remediation) for critical incidents.
- A clear incident-credit schedule (how credits scale with downtime and severity).

Can you share a commit-linked pricing ladder (monthly committed token or GPU-hour tiers) with the associated uptime/response SLAs and any introductory discounts for a 12-month commitment? Also flag any hard limits (seat counts, max burst capacity) that would affect pricing.

Elena
Elena Morris
Head of Platform Ops | Skyward Analytics
elena.morris@skywardanalytics.com
+1 415 555 0192

--
Attachment: rfx_attachment_v1.pdf (referenced in procurement brief)
From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@skywardanalytics.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 11:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA packaging options for enterprise commit

Hi Elena — great to meet yesterday. Appreciate the clear asks. Below is a compact proposal that maps commit tiers to SLA/response coverage; happy to walk through in a short call.

Summary (commit-linked response ladder):
- Bronze (baseline) — 0 (no commit) / Self-serve: 99.90% availability SLA; P1 ack within 4 hours; no guaranteed remediation window; incident credit: 5% of monthly invoice for qualifying downtime.
- Silver (recommended for pilots) — 2,000 committed GPU-hours/mo: 99.925% availability; P1 ack within 2 hours; target remediation 12 hours; incident credits escalate to 10% for Severity 1 events >30 min. 5% volume discount when commit >= 3 months.
- Gold (enterprise) — 10,000 committed GPU-hours/mo: 99.95% availability; P1 ack within 1 hour; target remediation 4 hours; on-call escalation (phone pager) included; incident credits up to 25% based on duration/severity. 12-month commit -> additional 7.5% discount.

Optional add-ons:
- Canary fallback routing (cross-region) — $X/month (reduces impact window, recommended for critical pipelines).
- Onboarding + runbook build: one-time fee (or one-month credit at Gold).
- Extended on-call (US-based 24x7) — +15% of support fee.

We attach a compact pricing grid and an incident credit schedule for visibility. Two things to note:
1) The uptime SLOs assume KV cache consistency expectations documented in the SLA appendix — cross-region failover will reduce observed impact but is billed separately.
2) For short pilot validations we can run a 30-day discounted Silver pilot (50% discount on support fee) to validate response and tooling.

Next steps: if this aligns, Ben can draft a canaryable contract with the commit bands and DocuSign-ready terms. Would Elena/Procurement like a brief review call tomorrow?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
+1 650 555 0146

Attachments: support_pricing_grid.pdf, incident_credit_schedule.xlsx
From: Elena Morris <elena.morris@skywardanalytics.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@skywardanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA packaging options for enterprise commit

Irene — thanks, this is helpful and straightforward. A few follow-ups from procurement and platform: 

1) Uptime target: Gold at 99.95% is close to what we need, but our executive team needs to see the incident credit math mapped to a multi-month trend (not just per-event). Can you add a 6-month rolling credit cap scenario?

2) Response windows: the P1 ack + 1-hr target remediation is good, but we need guaranteed escalations to our named on-call within 30 minutes for P1s during business hours. Is that something you can commit to for Gold?

3) Credits vs. Service Credits: procurement prefers credits applied as service credit (applied to the monthly invoice) rather than refunds. Confirm we can accept credits that roll forward to offset future invoices.

4) Discount ask: If we commit at Gold + a 24-month term, can Redwood increase the term discount to 12% and include one month of free onboarding (to cover runbook/workshop)?

Finally — we're open to the 30-day Silver pilot, but procurement asks for a capped incident liability during the pilot (e.g., max credit = 20% of pilot support fee).

Can Ben or Marissa put together an updated schedule that includes a 6-month aggregation cap and the 24-month term uplift? Also please call out any limitations around third-party cloud marketplace billing if we take the contract through our AWS marketplace channel.

Elena

---

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: Elena Morris <elena.morris@skywardanalytics.com>
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: SLA packaging options for enterprise commit

Elena — thanks for the clear asks and the hire-level constraints. Quick counter and commitment constructs that should address procurement concerns: 

- Aggregated credits: we can provide a 6-month rolling credit cap (example table attached) — credits will be issued as service credits applied to future invoices, per your preference.

- Named on-call escalation: for Gold, we commit to escalation to a named engineer within 30 minutes during business hours (PST 7am-7pm). For 24x7 named escalation, we offer the extended on-call add-on (+15% support fee).

- Term uplift: 24-month Gold commitment -> 12% support discount + one month onboarding credit applied at contract start. We will also include an explicit limitation of liability clause for pilot periods (cap: 20% of pilot support fee).

- Marketplace billing: if you plan to route via AWS marketplace, pricing is functionally identical but we have to add a small reseller fee (typically 3-5%) due to marketplace commissions; we can produce a marketplace invoice option that keeps the effective pass-through discount aligned with your ask.

Next: I will update the incident credit schedule (xlsx) to show the 6-month rolling aggregation and produce a DocuSign-ready addendum reflecting the 24-month uplift + onboarding credit. If you like, we can start the Silver pilot next Monday and then convert to Gold with a mid-term review in month 2.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow 10:00am PT to lock the terms? If so, I'll send a calendar invite and the DocuSign link for the term sheet.

Best,
Ben Carter
